name: Wholesale Gorilla
summary: B2B wholesale inside an ordinary Shopify store: custom prices per customer group, a signup and approval flow, net payment terms, wholesale-only shipping rules and a quick-order form, so trade buyers order from the same storefront as retail customers. Nothing is metered: the three tiers gate features, not volume. Read on the App Store and the vendor's own comparison chart on 8 September 2026.
best_for: Shopify merchants who already have wholesale buyers and want them ordering from the same store as retail customers: custom price groups, a signup and approval flow, net terms and wholesale-only shipping rules: without moving up to Shopify Plus for native B2B.
skip_if: you need one flat wholesale percentage and nothing else, which customer tags and a far cheaper app already cover; you are on Shopify Plus, where native B2B gives you price lists and payment terms without a second subscription; or you want volume-break pricing on a small budget, because that single feature costs $149.95 a month here.
honest_knock: It is a feature ladder, not a volume ladder, and the features most people picture when they say wholesale sit high on it. Volume discounts (buy ten, pay less each) are Premium only, at $149.95 a month, more than four times the entry price. Discount codes, net payment terms, wholesale shipping rules and theme integration all start at Advanced, $69.95. Lite at $34.95 buys custom prices per customer group and a basic signup form, which is a price list rather than a wholesale channel. Work out which rung you actually need before you read $34.95 as your price, because the honest entry point for most wholesale operations is the middle one.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/wholesale-gorilla and in our own test that day; earlier: read 2026-09-08 and re-read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/wholesale-gorilla and checked against the vendor's own plan-comparison page at wholesalegorilla.com/plan-comparison/, which lists the same three figures) Three tiers, all billed in USD every 30 days: Lite $34.95 a month, Advanced $69.95 and Premium $149.95. There is no free plan. Every tier carries a 21-day free trial and nothing beyond it, so budget from day 22. Nothing here is metered — pricing rules and customer price groups are unlimited on all three tiers — so what you are buying as you climb is features, not volume. The app has been on the Shopify App Store since 26 September 2018 and on 19 September 2026 showed 4.8 stars over 317 reviews — 275 five-star, 17 four, 8 three, 5 two and 12 one — up from 4.7 over 313 eleven days earlier. Its Works with field names only Checkout, customer accounts and Shopify Admin. Read again on 17 November 2026: the three amounts, the 21 day free trial and the absence of a free plan are unchanged on the listing, and the rating block read 4.8 over 321 reviews. The Lite card on the listing no longer names Shopify Markets among its features, which our earlier plan list did. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the install dialog warned that Wholesale Gorilla does not support market driven shipping. Choosing Lite opened Shopify's approval screen: $34.95 every 30 days after a 21 day trial ending 8 December, with the line “You will not be billed for this test charge”. We uninstalled the app without approving it.

compare_with.name: Shopify Plus native B2B
compare_with.why: Shopify's own B2B is included once you are on Plus, and it puts company accounts, price lists and payment terms in the platform itself rather than in an app that sits on top of your theme. Wholesale Gorilla exists for the shops below that line: it brings the same shape of wholesale to a standard Shopify plan for $34.95 to $149.95 a month, which is a fraction of the step up to Plus. The trade is where the logic lives. Native B2B cannot break when a theme updates; an app that integrates with your theme can, and the recurring complaint in this app's own reviews is exactly that: updates and theme changes that interrupt checkout. If you are already on Plus, paying again for this is hard to justify.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session installed Wholesale Gorilla on a Shopify development store. The app opened on its plan screen and the price rules only open after a plan is approved; the Shopify approval screen for Lite said there would be no charge for this test but also showed an Add payment method row, so it was not approved and the wholesale pricing was not tested. The app was uninstalled; nothing was paid. Install: the install form was sent at about 22:24 in our own tab. The dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, with the warning Wholesale Gorilla doesn't support market-driven shipping; it was approved at about 22:25. Core action NOT DONE: the app opened at once on its plan screen (21-day FREE trial for all plans) and the price rules only open after a plan is chosen. No wholesale price, customer tag or sign-up form was made. Plans in the app: Lite $34.95, Advanced $69.95 (popular) and Premium $149.95 a month, as on the listing. Checkout: Start selling wholesale on Lite opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the line You will not be billed for this test charge, plan Lite, $34,95 USD every 30 days, a 21-day free trial ending on 8 Dec, total $34,95 due 8 Dec and a row Add payment method. Our rule is to approve nothing on a screen with an Add payment method row, so nothing was approved and no card was entered. Cancelling: no subscription existed. The uninstall dialog Uninstall Wholesale Gorilla? warns that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and needs a reason (Testing multiple apps). Clean up: the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps and is gone from Installed. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app shows nothing but a plan screen until a plan is approved; the approval screen said there would be no charge for this test but still showed an Add payment method row; the install dialog warns that the app does not support market-driven shipping.
